name: Albemarle Corporation
moat_justification: Tier-1 low-cost assets (Salar de Atacama brine, Greenbushes hard-rock JV, leading bromine position) give a real structural cost advantage, but Albemarle is a commodity price-taker with no pricing power: ROIC (fundamentals.json roic_proxy) ran 8.8% / 6.1% / 8.2% / 21.4% / 1.6% / -11.4% / -2.6% across FY2019-FY2025 — above the cost of capital only in the 2022 lithium spike — and gross margin swung from 42.0% (FY2022) to 1.2% (FY2024) and 13.0% (FY2025). A cost curve position that cannot defend returns through the cycle is a weak-to-moderate moat: 4/10.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED: the only cash tag filed for the latest fiscal year is the combined cash + restricted-cash total and no restricted-cash tag separates it — net debt is UNDERSTATED by the restricted amount (escrow / collateral / regulatory); check the balance sheet before trusting HIGH_NET_DEBT's absence
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 6.9x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (8.0%) vs bull-case tier B (17.7%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Cost-advantaged lithium/bromine producer, moat 4/10 — TTM owner's earnings recovered to $9.58/share on the lithium rebound, but through-cycle ROIC is weak and the commodity decides the outcome (bear Tier D at 8.0% to bull Tier B at 17.7%); weighted IRR 12.7% (weighted IV@15% $77.73 vs the $95.48 price), so it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$78.
moat_for: Salar de Atacama (Chile) brine and Greenbushes (Australia, JV) hard-rock stake — among the lowest-cost, highest-quality lithium resources in the world
Leading global bromine position (Jordan / Arkansas) with steadier pricing — Specialties Q2 2026 sales +20.5% YoY, adjusted EBITDA +61.3%
Scale and technical know-how in lithium conversion; long-term contracts cover ~40% of lithium salts volume
Balance sheet repaired in the trough: capex cut from $2,154M (FY2023) to $590M (FY2025), $1.3B of debt repaid in Q1 2026, Ketjen 51% stake sold
moat_against: Pure price-taker: realized lithium price swung from the 2022 spike to ~$10/kg in 2025 and back to $19.53/kg realized in Q2 2026 — earnings follow the commodity, not the franchise
Through-cycle ROIC below the cost of capital in most years (FY2023 1.6%, FY2024 -11.4%, FY2025 -2.6%); gross margin 42.0% -> 1.2% peak-to-trough
Chinese / African supply overhang and lepidolite capacity cap lithium prices; new supply is the bear case's engine
Heavy sustaining/growth capex in expansions: capex of $2,154M in FY2023 against OCF of $1,327M produced negative owner's earnings at the trough
CORFO commissions and Chilean fiscal take rise with lithium prices, skimming the upside at Atacama
